column3: Near formulation; identifies the later abode as the living reality beyond diversion.
Adds the instability of deeds detached from the Lord, extending the warning beyond present appearance.
Offers a boundary case where failure to reason sustains invented religious claims.
Sets temporary worldly enjoyment against the abiding abode, sharpening the duration contrast.
Shows entrenched perception as a barrier to receiving the warning, without stating the life contrast.
Boundary evidence: play can name an ordinary proposed activity, not automatically the condemned condition.
Joins worldly adornment, greater endurance, and reason in a close parallel to the focus.
Locates play in heedless reception of reminder, specifying one mode of diversion.
Restates play and diversion while joining faith and taqwa to recompense.
Confirms the later reward as better for faith and taqwa, though it adds little after earlier parallels.
Connects faith and reform with a consequence horizon, indirectly supporting the focus's conduct side.
Contrasts immediate gain with the later abode and exposes rationalization of repeated taking.
Preserves worldly good while ranking the later abode higher, qualifying a total rejection of the present.
Adds an irreversible-return boundary, only indirectly related to the focus's destination.
Combines historical outcomes, the better later abode, taqwa, and reason.
Reinforces the temporary-versus-enduring comparison, now with faith and reliance.
Supports correction of false attribution but adds no direct account of play, afterlife, or taqwa.
Makes lack of taqwa visible in recurring covenant breach, giving behavioral texture to the focus.
Expands diversion into adornment, rivalry, accumulation, decay, and delusive provision.
Offers a guided-route parallel, but no clear addition to the focus's contrast.
Makes taqwa concrete as guarding self and household against an ultimate consequence.
Links reason to a messenger's non-transactional call, only a remote support for the focus.
Stresses that later recognition cannot replace prior faith and acquired good.
Supplies a fulfilled historical promise, with no direct worldly/afterlife comparison.
Adds mortality, final recompense, and the world's delusive provision in one framing.
The arrogance scene has no usable addition to the focus despite auxiliary resonance.
Names a peace-filled abode joined to deeds, giving a positive destination image.
The isolated appeal to reason lacks enough local content to add a distinct reading.
Places fear of the great day within the same surah's warning horizon.
Associates the Arabic Quran with reasoning, but does not develop the focus's contrast.
Holds present and later good together and associates mercy with taqwa.
The celestial-motion scene supplies no clear interpretive addition here.
Applies taqwa to speech and conduct before return; the contrast link marks a boundary, not support.
Frames reminder as oriented toward taqwa and accountability within the focus's surah.
Shows that even intensified signs may not overcome refusal, qualifying reason as mere exposure.
Treats making worship into play as linked with failure to reason, a concrete misuse of the terms.
Directly connects taking religion as diversion with worldly deception and forgetting the appointed meeting.
Compresses life, death, and return into the destination horizon underlying the focus.
Uses created order as material for reasoning, but remains a generic support.
Limits coercive worldly rule, giving a concrete temporal-power contrast.
Addresses guidance and fear in context but adds no distinct worldly/afterlife articulation.
Begins the conduct pattern of giving and taqwa; parallel and contrast readings remain boundary evidence.
A generic call to taqwa adds little after more developed conduct examples.
Makes acquired acts answerable in an equitable final accounting.
Applies taqwa to communal restraint; its contrast route is boundary evidence only.
Within the same surah, joins religion-as-play, worldly deception, personal acquisition, and consequence.
Establishes certainty through a vision of dominion but does not specify the focus's valuation.
Presents signs for reasoning without a distinct present/later or diversional claim.
Directly ranks worldly enjoyment as a limited provision in relation to the later reality.
Life, death, and renewed life support the focus's destination horizon without its ethical contrast.
Uses reason against false worship, a broad but indirect corrective.
Sets luxury as present provision and reserves the later outcome for the mindful.
The wish to return after confronting Fire gives the focus's warning concrete retrospective force.
Shows religion treated as mockery and play while retaining taqwa as the response.
Contrasts present adornment with enduring righteous acts, adding an alternative object of hope.
The dead/living and resurrection contrast supports the later-life horizon indirectly.
Grounds the rejection of play in purposeful creation rather than merely human conduct.
Supplies measured recompense for deeds, but the present/later contrast is unstated.
Shares the surah's rejection setting without adding the focus's valuation or conduct logic.
A remaining sign for reason is too general to advance the earlier developed reading.
Gives the later abode an ethical profile: no exaltation or corruption, with taqwa as outcome.
The announced action against idols has no clear addition to the focus.
Keeps taqwa and forgiveness together while preserving divine willing as a boundary.
Contrasts present disgrace with a greater later consequence, extending the temporal scale.
Prophetic endurance supplies context for warning but not the focus's central contrast.
A generic closing appeal to reason adds no particular content.
Relates affliction and guided hearts, only remotely connected to long-horizon valuation.
The hearing metaphor and auxiliary routes do not yield a clear addition to the focus.
Makes taqwa an enduring condition carried through death, though it is otherwise generic.
Diagnoses attention to the outward present alongside heedlessness of the later reality.
The demand for a sign shares the surah's setting but adds no distinct focus reading.
Defines play as conduct within doubt, adding an epistemic form of diversion.
States the later as better than the earlier, but is highly compressed and now redundant.
Links denial of the later life with unfounded claims and desire-following in the same surah.
The prayer for destruction has no usable addition to the focus.
Sets a harder later punishment beyond present punishment, strengthening the consequence horizon.
Ties warning of gathering to taqwa and lack of other protection within the focus's surah.
Tests a claim about the later abode but does not develop the focus's values.
Directly rebukes choosing earthly attachment and measures its provision against the later life.
Supplies an accountability and intent scene but no distinct present/later or diversion reading.
A concise warning to guard against Fire adds little beyond earlier concrete taqwa passages.
Identifies preferring worldly life over the later one as the decisive reversed valuation.
Affirms exclusive devotion and submission, without a specific addition to the focus.
Uses the play/seriousness opposition as a boundary for receiving truth.
Names preference for worldly life as a concise opposing pole, though the surrounding outcome is absent.
The dietary restriction and its context offer no clear addition to the focus.
Points to the eventual outcome of the abode, but remains too nonspecific after earlier parallels.
Shows exchange of the later life for the worldly one and its uncompensated consequence.
A destruction outcome in the surah does not itself explain play, afterlife, or taqwa.
Extends taqwa across what lies ahead and behind, but remains a generic exhortation.
The isolated group reference has no interpretable addition without omitted context.
A generic command to taqwa and obedience adds no new focus-specific content.
Purposeful creation rejects play, but this repeats the earlier creation parallel with less addition.
Applies taqwa to a social obligation, only indirectly illustrating its conduct dimension.
Places worldly provision before return and severe consequence, a late but direct temporal sequence.
Associates rescue with faith and taqwa but adds no distinct valuation or horizon.
Shows consequences of prior acts and retrospective excuse-making, indirectly related at most.
An isolated call to taqwa is fully redundant after the developed readings.
Frames present acts as stored with God for a better and greater reward.
Shows protection from a plot and punishment for its makers, but no direct focus addition.
Contrasts a horizon restricted to the present with having no share in the later one.
Supplies a balancing boundary by seeking good in both present and later horizons.
Sets worldly attraction and mockery against the elevation of the mindful at final judgment.
Explicitly joins reflection on the present world and the later one.
Catalogues attractive present desires and redirects comparison toward what is better with God.
Pairs the better divine outcome with taqwa, closely developing the focus's destination.
Keeps present and later recompense distinct, preventing the reward horizon from collapsing into one sphere.
Shows both present reward and a better later reward, again preserving a non-totalizing contrast.
Marks present enjoyment as brief before a decisive later consequence.
Frames action as exchange of the present life for the later one.
Directly calls present enjoyment small and the later reality better, with accountability protection.
Names transitory worldly gain as a temptation within committed action.
Locates the rewards of both worlds with God, qualifying short-term reward seeking.
Provides a boundary against treating present adornment itself as forbidden or worthless.
Makes wealth and children a test, supplying a concrete pressure within the present life.
Contrasts a desire for immediate worldly goods with the divine orientation toward the later outcome.
Names loved possessions and settled life as attachments that can displace a higher commitment.
Diagnoses contentment with the present and settledness in it as heedlessness of the larger horizon.
Limits worldly enjoyment by placing return after it.
Uses the rapid fading of worldly flourishing to make the focus's impermanence concrete.
Distinguishes those seeking present life and adornment from the later consequences of that choice.
States the null later yield of works confined to the present horizon.
Identifies preferring present life over the later one as a decisive inversion of value.
Pairs a good present settlement with a greater later reward, preserving both levels.
Contrasts what ends in human possession with what remains with God.
Links a good present life with a superior recompense horizon for enduring good action.
Traces pursuit of the immediate to a limited grant and later loss.
Sets a deliberate later aim and faithful striving as the contrasting orientation.
Calls for comparison across ranks and declares the later distinctions greater.
Names desire for worldly adornment as a force that can turn attention from remembrance.
Gives a fading-growth parable for the instability of worldly life.
Treats worldly splendor as a test rather than a final measure of worth.
Places worldly good and evil under testing and return, broadening the focus's accountability horizon.
Explicitly joins loss in the present and the later life as the result of unstable commitment.
Preserves the contrary claim that confines life to the present and denies resurrection.
Contrasts an assured good promise with temporary worldly provision before final presentation.
Directs use of what is given toward the later abode while retaining a present share as a boundary.
Shows how visible worldly splendor generates envious valuation from observers.
Answers that valuation by preferring the divine reward for faith and righteous action.
Warns that worldly life can deceive, placing deception explicitly in the focus's field.
Sets choosing worldly life and adornment against a higher household commitment.
Completes that choice with God, the messenger, and the later abode as the alternative aim.
Warns directly against deception by worldly life.
Contrasts a present-world summons with the return that belongs to the later horizon.
Sets present humiliation against a more enduring later consequence.
Contrasts cultivation for the later harvest with cultivation confined to the present and its loss beyond it.
Preserves the contrary present-only account that denies any later horizon.
Connects treating divine signs as mockery with deception by worldly life.
Shows present goods being exhausted before a humiliating later consequence.
Diagnoses a will directed only toward worldly life after turning from remembrance.
Supplies the positive counter-movement: racing toward forgiveness and a garden.
Places an immediate punishment beside a prepared later punishment.
Names wealth and children as distractions from remembrance, a concrete form of diversion.
Marks wealth and children as a test, reinforcing but not completing the focus's warning.
Compares a present punishment with a greater later punishment.
Names love of the immediate as the opposing orientation.
Completes that opposition by naming abandonment of the later horizon.
Contrasts attachment to the immediate with neglect of a weighty day ahead.
Adds transgression as part of the pattern that culminates in choosing present life.
Sets fear of standing before the Lord and restraint of desire as the focus's behavioral counterforce.
Names the final refuge attached to that restraint, completing the contrast unit.
Directly names preference for the present life as the contrary choice.
States that the later reality is better and more enduring.
Names competitive accumulation as a form of distraction, closely paralleling the focus's diversion.
Carries that distraction to the grave boundary, exposing its terminal horizon.
